nodes.label: Liquid Glass Modals & Full-Screen Titlebar Design
nodes.rationale: Move-to popup and Collection editor used native .sheet()/NavigationStack/.toolbar chrome that renders the OS's generic opaque toolbar directly above already-glassy content, an inconsistency with the app's other overlay-based modals (SnippetDetailView/SnippetEditorView); goal is to reuse the existing liquidGlassSurface/DSGlassContainer vocabulary rather than invent new primitives.
nodes.norm_label: liquid glass modals & full-screen titlebar design

nodes.label: Settings Window Redesign & Disintegration Smoothness Design
nodes.rationale: Settings window used a stock TabView/.formStyle(.grouped) that clashed with the app's de-chromed glass modals; the disintegration effect looked choppy because frame delivery was coupled to SwiftUI's TimelineView (not v-synced, capped at 60Hz, delayed by main-thread layout), particle identity was unstable (progress-dependent cellSize re-binned pixels every frame), and per-frame random flicker/high-frequency flutter made motion read as jitter rather than drift.
nodes.norm_label: settings window redesign & disintegration smoothness design

nodes.label: fragment_main (dissolve shader)
nodes.rationale: Uses a constant cellSize (not progress-dependent) to keep particle identity stable across frames, keys all per-particle randomness to the stable cell id (never moving coordinates) to avoid flicker, and drives motion via per-particle local time (smoothstep window of global progress) so the dissolve frontier sweeps smoothly while individual particles animate coherently.
